overview: The Community Preservation Committee (CPC) manages Medford's Community Preservation Act (CPA) funds, allocating resources toward open space, historic preservation, and affordable housing. Meeting regularly since at least July 2024, the committee evaluates applications from both municipal departments and private community organizations through an annual funding cycle. Major projects supported include park renovations, the restoration of historic municipal and religious buildings, and seed funding for the city's Affordable Housing Trust. The committee also maintains a small grant program for lower-cost projects and handles emergency restoration requests for historic structures. As of October 2026, the body is reviewing a new slate of fiscal year 2027 applications and exploring a long-term funding strategy for the Medford High School construction project.

threads.name: Park and Open Space Improvements
threads.summary: The committee manages significant investments in city parks, including a $146,000 recommendation for Carr Park Phase 2 and $526,000 for Playstead Park tennis court reconstruction. Funding was also allocated for lighting at the Condon Shell and Tufts Park Field 2, with the committee later considering budget pivots to cover rising material costs. Ongoing projects include a digital scoreboard at Playstead Park and a $264,000 request for Victory Park athletic courts.

threads.name: Historic Preservation of Religious Buildings
threads.summary: CPC frequently funds the restoration of historic church structures, provided the work adheres to preservation standards and avoids religious imagery. Notable projects include a $400,000 recommendation for ADA improvements at Shiloh Baptist Church and multiple phases of window restoration at the same site. The committee also approved $99,000 for the Unitarian Universalist Church siding and $10,000 for the Osgood House.

citations.title: Shiloh Baptist Church Window Restoration Phase 2
citations.label: M11#5

threads.name: Municipal Building Restoration
threads.summary: The committee evaluates requests to maintain and restore historic city-owned assets, such as City Hall and the Medford Armory. While the committee denied an HVAC request for a fire station because it lacked historic windows, it recommended $322,500 for the City Hall Council Chambers window restoration. Emergency masonry repairs were approved for the Armory, and the committee is currently reviewing a $300,000 request for City Hall facade restoration.

citations.label: M01#3

citations.title: City Hall Council Chambers Window Restoration Approval

threads.name: Affordable Housing and Social Services
threads.summary: The body provides financial support to the Medford Affordable Housing Trust, including an initial $250,000 for pre-development work and operations. Other housing initiatives include the ABCD move-in assistance program for low-income households and updates on the Walkling Court redevelopment. The committee also deliberated on the administrative complexity of funding a private affordable accessory dwelling unit.

citations.label: M08#5

citations.title: ABCD Medford Move In Medford Move Forward
citations.label: M12#1

threads.name: Cemetery and Monument Preservation
threads.summary: Preservation of cemetery buildings and monuments is a recurring priority, with recommendations for headstone restoration at Cross Street Cemetery and planning for buildings at Oak Grove Cemetery. The committee supported the $167,800 restoration of the Angel of Victory and Peace Fountain. Large-scale bonding for cemetery structures remains a point of discussion regarding the city's long-term strategic plan.

citations.title: Angel of Victory and Peace Fountain Restoration
citations.label: M11#3

threads.name: Administrative and Policy Development
threads.summary: The committee continuously refines its governance, establishing a $5,000 threshold for administrative fund approvals and creating guidelines for private property preservation. In 2025, the committee doubled the small grant limit to $10,000 and removed the mandatory matching requirement to increase accessibility. It also updated application materials to simplify the process for city departments and added requirements for public event hosting at funded sites.

threads.name: Medford High School Project Funding
threads.summary: A new line of work emerged in mid-2026 regarding potential CPA funding for non-reimbursable components of the Medford High School construction project. The committee formed a subcommittee to evaluate how to support items like playgrounds, fields, and site trees through multi-year funding and bonding.

periods.narrative: This period focused on the first major round of project recommendations under new membership and the establishment of core administrative policies and grant limits.
During this term, the committee continued its annual funding cycles while beginning long-term planning for the Medford High School construction project.
